subject: Civil Engineering
title: River Channel Engineering
description: A quick win: understand River Channel Engineering.

hook.text: Straighten a river and it flows faster. Faster water means flooding moves downstream.

buildup.text: Channelization deepens, widens, or straightens rivers to increase their carrying capacity.

discovery.text: Riprap — loose stone — lines channel banks to prevent erosion from fast-moving water.

twist.text: Channelized rivers lose habitat. Fish disappear. Downstream communities flood instead.

climax.text: River restoration projects now restore meanders — undoing 20th-century channelization.

punchline.text: Straighten a river and someone else floods. Restore its curves and everyone benefits.

quiz.question: Why is river channelization often criticized today?
options: It is too expensive compared to other flood control methods
It speeds up flow, destroying habitat and shifting flooding downstream
It makes rivers too deep for recreational boating
